concepts.def: An organised, persistent store of data.
Rows are records; columns are fields.
A field that uniquely identifies each record.
Language to query and manage a relational database.
A request to select or change data.

walkthroughs.body_html: A Books table has BookID (primary key). A Loans table has BookID as a foreign key pointing back to Books. This means each loan is tied to exactly one book without duplicating book details.

SELECT name, year FROM Students WHERE year = 11;

This returns the name and year columns for all rows where the year is 11.

SELECT * FROM Books WHERE author = 'Orwell' AND year > 1945;

The * returns every column; AND requires both conditions to be true.
